It was explicitly stated that genderimplications were not part of the experiment.Of course, gender was part of past research in the domain of virtual assistants: Kim et al. [7] studiedthe effects of gender and relationship type on conversational Agents and concluded no significant effectsof gender regarding competence, warmth or pleasure. It was stated, that this is contrary to past research.The experiment also studied casual conversation with voice agents, not embodiment or solving of tasks.The effects on gender when helping in a quiz assignment was studied with text-chat-based agents by Pfeuf-fer et al. Variables affecting perception and competence of gendered technology were identifiedin the research, with the comment that future research can explore these variables in an experimental approach.
